title: window.ml program manifest
description: A program manifest (docs/spec/PROGRAM_MANIFEST.md): how window.ml describes a call to one program, per subcommand and flag. GENERATED from shell/program-manifest.ts by scripts/gen-export-schema.mjs — do not edit by hand. The TypeScript file is normative for the fields and the validator in it is the authority for what is accepted; this schema is the editor's view of both (hints, and the rules JSON Schema can state).

$schema.description: An editor hint (a JSON Schema URL or path) and nothing else: ignored by `describeCall` and by the host's reader (window-ml-host's `manifest.rs` denies unknown fields and would refuse a file carrying it). The shipped manifests do not have one; a manifest you write for your own use may.

program.description: The program's name: the basename of `argv[0]` must equal it.

okCodes.description: Exit codes that count as success besides 0, for every command of the program.

echoes.description: The program prints the environment or its inputs back (`curl -v`).

env.description: Environment variables that change what the program does: a call setting one is not described.

command.description: The program's top-level command: its effects, path operands, flags and subcommands.

version.description: A standalone binary's pin: the version range the manifest was written against, and how the host reads the program's version. Exclusive with `entrypoint`.

entrypoint.description: An interpreted script's pin: its path under a workspace root and the sha256 of the resolved file; `program` is then the interpreter. Exclusive with `version`.

CommandSpec.description: A program or one of its subcommands.

effects.description: What the command does with no flags, applied to its path targets.

paths.description: Which operands are paths: none, all, all from an index on, or the repository (the cwd, or a `valueIsDir` flag's value).

noPaths.description: What the command touches when it is given no path operand: the cwd (`ls`, `rg`), or nothing (stdin: `cat`).

terminator.description: The end-of-options marker the command honours, where the host puts it before a value from a variable.

maxOperands.description: At most this many operands; more makes the call `unknown` (`git branch` lists with none, creates with one).

flags.description: Every flag the command accepts, by its spelling (`-r`, `--recursive`, `-name`). One absent here makes the call `unknown`.

subcommands.description: The first operand selects one; an unlisted one makes the call `unknown`.

primaries.description: For `syntax: "find"`: every primary and operator; an unlisted one makes the call `unknown`.

okCodes.description: Exit codes that are answers, not failures, for this command (`grep`-style: 1 is "no match"). Added to the program's own.

echoes.description: It prints the environment or its inputs back.

recursive.description: It walks its directory arguments (`rg`, `find`): the host checks what is beneath them for secrets.

optionsFirst.description: GNU permutes options and operands (`rm a -r` is recursive); BSD stops at the first operand (`rm a -r` removes two files). An argument starting with `-` after an operand, `--` included, makes the call `unknown`.

dashIsPath.description: A lone `-` is a FILE NAME here (`rm -` removes the file `-`), not stdin: it stays a path operand.

repoWide.description: The command may reach anything in its repository, whatever its operands say (`git rm` removes the parent directories it empties; `git mv` creates names under a directory): its effects also fall on the directory it acts in and on the repository's root (`resolve({arg: "repo"})`).

pathspecs.description: Operands are git pathspecs: one that starts with `:` (magic; `:/x` is relative to the repository root, not to the cwd) is not a path the host can resolve, so the call is `unknown`.

harden.description: Arguments the caller inserts right after this command's name, turning off what the repository's own config could make it run (`git` → `--no-pager`; `git diff` → `--no-ext-diff --no-textconv`). They never widen a call.

FlagSpec.description: One flag of a command: whether it takes a value, and what it adds to the call. A flag absent from its command's table makes the call `unknown`.

value.description: Takes one value: `--f=v`, `--f v`, `-fv` or `-f v`.

optionalValue.description: Takes a value only in the attached form (`--color=always`); the bare flag is also valid.

effects.description: Effects the flag adds, in the program-manifest vocabulary.

valueIsPath.description: The flag's value is a path the program reads or writes (`--output=f`, `--contents f`).

valueIsDir.description: The flag's value is the directory the command acts in, instead of the cwd (`git -C dir`).

pathsFrom.description: With this flag, path operands start at this index instead of the command's own (`rg -e pat a b`: 0).

runner.description: It starts another program (`find -exec`, `git -c core.pager=…`): never free on the program's word.

echoes.description: It prints the environment or its inputs back (`curl -v`).

okCodes.description: Exit codes that become answers with this flag (`git diff --exit-code`: 1).

recursive.description: With this flag the command walks its directory arguments (`ls -R`).

PrimarySpec.description: A `find`-style expression primary: how many arguments it consumes (or up to which terminator), and what it adds.

until.description: Consumes arguments up to and including one of these (`-exec … ;` or `+`).

effects.description: Effects the primary adds, in the program-manifest vocabulary.

argIsPath.description: Its (first) argument is a path the program reads or writes (`-newer f`, `-fprint f`).

runner.description: It starts another program (`-exec`, `-ok`): its effects include `runs-code` or `unknown`.

ManifestVersion.description: The version range a binary's manifest was written against (`>=2.30.0 <3`) and how the host reads the version (`args`, a regex whose group 1 is it). `"*"` with no `args` is a program that reports no version (BSD `ls`, `find`): its manifest then lists only flags whose meaning is the same in every implementation.

range.description: Space-separated comparators that must all hold (`>=2.30.0 <3`), or `"*"` for a program that reports no version.

args.description: The arguments that make the program print its version; empty for `"*"`.

pattern.description: A regex whose group 1 is the version in that output; empty for `"*"`.

ManifestEntrypoint.description: An interpreted script's pin (`node scripts/index.mjs`): `path` relative to a workspace root, `sha256` of the resolved file.

path.description: The script, relative to a workspace root: no leading `/` or `-`, no `.`, `..` or empty segment.

sha256.description: The lowercase hex SHA-256 of the resolved file.

ProgramEffect.description: A program manifest's effect term: what a command, flag or primary does to its path targets (docs/spec/PROGRAM_MANIFEST.md).
